In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterisation of genes involved in the AM symbiosis.
the expression patterns and the differential transcript levels of Pi transporter genes in roots of M. truncatual inoculated by different AM fungi.
the identification of genes that are specifically induced by the interaction with AM fungi, by phosphate or by phytohormonal treatments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AM fungi have a strong influence on the transcript levels of genes involved in phosphate uptake, but that this is not a general feature of all mycorrhizas.
the AM fungi G. rosea (and probably also Glomus species) and the Pi supply have a similar effect on root gene expression, while the effect of phytohormonal treatments differs significantly.
there are no common genes that are regulated by AM fungi and phytohorns, but there is a common response to Pi in roots inoculated by AM fungi and roots fertilised with phosphate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the AM fungus Gigaspora rosa induces a large number of genes that are commonly regulated by Pi fertilisation, while there is little overlap between the AM fungi Gigaspora rosa, Glomus mossea and Glomus intra radices.
AM fungi induce similar sets of genes in M. truncata roots but the expression patterns of these genes are dependent on the fungal species.
the AM fungus Gomus rosea has a unique effect on gene expression in M. truncataula roots, which is reflected by its unique effect on phosphate nutrition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AM fungal colonisation induces a specific transcriptional programme that is not shared by other symbiotic interactions, such as those with rhizobia or with phytohormonal treatments.
the AM fungi can be grouped into different functional categories based on their ability to regulate the expression of genes involved in phosphate transport.
AM fungi differ in the way they affect the transcriptome of host roots, which might be linked to differences in phosphate nutrition.
